name: KNIFE MILL
desc: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS INNO-KM-200 Knife Mill (Blender) is predominantly used in agriculture, food testing, and forensic laboratories. It is engineered for the rapid size reduction and homogenization of soft, elastic, fibrous, and high-moisture samples like meat, plant leaves, seeds, and chocolate. It features interval, regular, and reverse modes for optimal mixing.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Knife Mill operates on the principle of high-speed mechanical size reduction through impact, cutting, and shearing forces. A high-speed electric motor drives specially designed stainless steel or titanium-coated cutting blades inside a grinding chamber. As the blades rotate, the sample undergoes repeated cutting, tearing, and mechanical impact, resulting in particle size reduction and homogeneous sample preparation. The combination of blade geometry, rotational speed, processing time, and operating mode determines the final particle size and homogenization efficiency. In analytical chemistry and research laboratories, the Knife Mill is particularly useful for preparing representative samples before chemical extraction, digestion, compositional analysis, and instrumental testing. In food chemistry, it is used for homogenizing meat, chocolate, cereals, seeds, spices, and other food matrices prior to moisture determination, fat extraction, protein estimation, and nutritional analysis. In agricultural and environmental research, it facilitates the preparation of leaves, roots, grains, seeds, and fibrous plant materials for subsequent extraction and analysis of pesticides, nutrients, minerals, pigments, and secondary metabolites. In forensic laboratories, suitable biological and material samples can be homogenized for subsequent validated analytical procedures. The interval mode allows intermittent processing to help manage sample heating, while reverse operation changes the blade rotation direction to assist with processing certain fibrous or difficult materials, where supported by the model. Regular operation provides continuous mechanical processing for appropriate samples. The instrument also supports dry and wet grinding, provided the sample composition, processing vessel, and cleaning requirements are compatible with the application. For research applications involving HPLC, GC-MS, UV-Visible spectroscopy, AAS, or ICP-OES, the Knife Mill improves sample homogeneity and helps obtain more representative analytical portions. It is important to understand that the instrument performs physical homogenization and does not independently carry out chemical extraction, digestion, sterilization, or molecular analysis.
sop: Place the Knife Mill on a stable, dry, level laboratory workbench with sufficient clearance around the equipment. Verify that the grinding chamber, cutting blades, sample container, power cable, and lid are clean and free from visible damage.

Check that the selected grinding container and blade assembly are appropriate for the sample type, batch quantity, and processing requirements. Ensure that the blades are securely fitted according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Ensure that the main power switch is in the OFF position before connecting the instrument to the electrical supply. Verify that the available supply matches the equipment rating of 220 V, 50 Hz, and that appropriate electrical earthing is available.

Prepare the sample by removing unsuitable foreign materials such as stones, metal pieces, glass fragments, and other contaminants. Cut oversized samples into appropriately sized portions compatible with the specified feed-size limit of the selected model.

Open the grinding chamber only after confirming that the motor and blades have completely stopped. Transfer the prepared sample into the container, keeping the quantity within the recommended batch capacity. Avoid overfilling the chamber because excessive loading can reduce grinding efficiency and strain the motor.
Secure the lid properly and verify that the electromagnetic safety lid lock or interlocking mechanism is engaged. Never attempt to operate the instrument with an improperly fitted lid.

Turn on the main switch and allow the control panel to initialize. Select the appropriate operating mode, such as Regular, Interval, or Reverse, according to the sample characteristics and the instrument's available functions.

Set the required operating time using the designated timer controls. On models equipped with a digital control panel, use the available SET button and UP/DOWN keys to adjust the processing time, then confirm the selection according to the panel instructions.

Select an appropriate rotational speed within the specified operating range of the particular model. Start the grinding cycle using the designated START or operating control and observe the instrument for unusual vibration, noise, or abnormal operation.

For fibrous, elastic, or moisture-rich samples, use the appropriate interval or reverse function where supported by the model. Allow suitable pauses between processing cycles when necessary to minimize excessive sample temperature and maintain sample quality.
After the grinding cycle finishes, switch off the motor and wait until the blades have come to a complete stop. Allow any suspended sample particles to settle before opening the lid.

Release the lid lock according to the manufacturer's instructions and carefully remove the homogenized sample using an appropriate clean laboratory spatula or sample-handling tool. Transfer the material into a properly labelled sample container for subsequent chemical or analytical procedures.

After completing the operation, switch off the main power supply and disconnect the instrument from the electrical outlet before cleaning. Remove sample residues using suitable cleaning materials and laboratory-approved cleaning procedures. Do not immerse the motor housing or electrical components in water.

Inspect the grinding chamber and blade assembly for retained sample residues, corrosion, or visible damage. Ensure that all cleaned components are completely dry before reassembly and subsequent storage.
Record the sample identification, batch quantity, selected operating mode, processing time, speed setting, and relevant observations in the laboratory instrument logbook.

SAFETY WARNING: The cutting blades are extremely sharp and can cause serious injuries. Never insert hands, fingers, spatulas, or cleaning tools into the grinding chamber while the instrument is connected to the power supply. Never bypass the electromagnetic lid interlock, open the lid during operation, or attempt to remove samples before complete blade stoppage. Always disconnect the power supply before cleaning or blade inspection, wear appropriate laboratory PPE, and never operate the equipment with a damaged blade assembly, defective safety lock, or unsecured lid.
features: Razor-sharp blades (Stainless Steel or Titanium coating/alloy)
High-speed motor adjustable from 500 up to 10000 rpm (Model dependent)
Coarse grinding and fine grinding realized in one step
Electromagnetic safety lid lock prevents opening during grinding
Supports dry as well as wet grinding applications

specifications.Operational Modes: Interval mode, Reverse mode, Press-and-play mode
specifications.Target Applications: Food Testing, Agriculture, Forensics, Meat & Plant Homogenization
